name: anf_polynomial_toffoli_cancellation
precondition: family = dv_recon (Toffoli-level IRCircuit, zero continuous Rz, measurement-free input); needs toffoli; qubits <= 20 so the whole-circuit judge still runs; the op list must contain at least one maximal classical-reversible segment, i.e. a contiguous run of ops drawn only from {x, cx, ccx, ccz, and h(q) pairs that sandwich a ccz on q and so read as ccx} containing >= 2 ccx/ccz, with no s/sdg/t/tdg and no unpaired h inside it. No ancillas, no measurement, no error drawn.
identity: Inside one classical-reversible segment, propagate the exact GF(2) algebraic normal form (ANF) of each wire. Initialise p_q = x_q (the segment's input variables). Then x(q): p_q ^= 1; cx(a,b): p_b ^= p_a; ccx(a,b -> t): p_t ^= p_a * p_b (polynomial product in GF(2)[x], squarefree-reduced by x^2 = x); ccz(a,b,c) is read as h(c) ccx(a,b -> c) h(c) wherever the sandwiching h's are present, otherwise left alone. Three rewrites, each applied to a single op and each exact: (R1) DEGENERATE CONTROL - if the ANF of p_a (or p_b) at that op's position is the constant 0, delete the ccx entirely; if it is the constant 1, replace ccx(a,b -> t) by cx(b,t) (resp. cx(a,t)). (R2) IDEMPOTENT CANCELLATION - if the monomial set of the product p_a * p_b is already a subset of the monomial set of p_t that was written by an EARLIER ccx(a',b' -> t) in the same segment with p_{a'} * p_{b'} == p_a * p_b (equal ANFs), and no op between the two writes any of the variables occurring in p_a, p_b, then both ccx ops are deleted and replaced by nothing: the two identical product terms XOR to 0. The intervening ops are unchanged because they never read t (checked) or read t only through further products that are recomputed from the restored ANF. (R3) LINEARISED PRODUCT - if p_a * p_b reduces, after squarefree reduction, to a polynomial of degree <= 1 (e.g. p_a == p_b, giving p_a * p_a = p_a, or p_a = 1 ^ p_b), replace the ccx by the equivalent Clifford net: a cx ladder realising p_t ^= (that affine form), i.e. cx's from the form's support plus one x if its constant is 1. Each fired rewrite removes one Toffoli, i.e. 7 T, and adds only x/cx/cz (0 T).
correctness: A segment of x/cx/ccx is a classical reversible map; its action on a computational basis state is exactly the simultaneous substitution of the per-wire ANFs, which is why propagating the ANF is a faithful (not approximate) symbolic execution of the segment. GF(2) arithmetic gives the three facts used: (i) 0 * p = 0 and 1 * p = p, so a control whose ANF is constant makes the Toffoli either the identity or a CNOT (R1); (ii) u ^ u = 0, so writing the same product twice into the same wire leaves it unchanged - deleting both writes yields the identical substitution map, hence the identical permutation unitary (R2), with the no-intervening-write side condition ensuring p_a, p_b have the same ANF at both positions; (iii) p * p = p over GF(2) under x^2 = x, and (1 ^ p) * p = p ^ p = 0, so products of dependent controls collapse to affine forms realisable by CNOT/X (R3). Because the segment is a permutation of basis states with no phases, equality of the substitution maps implies equality of the unitaries exactly - no global or relative phase is introduced, so invariants 1, 2 and 6 all hold and the frozen judge's exact D[omega] check on the changed window applies with zero ledger charge. The h(c)-ccz-h(c) reading is the standard CCX = H_t CCZ H_t identity, exact over Z[omega]; a ccz whose target is not H-sandwiched is simply not matched.
trigger: Walk the op list, cutting segments at any t/tdg/s/sdg, any measurement, and any h that is not the first or second member of an h(q) ... h(q) pair enclosing a ccz acting on q with no other op touching q in between. In each segment with >= 2 ccx/ccz, run the ANF propagation (dict wire -> frozenset of monomials, monomials as int bitmasks over the segment's input variables, constant 1 as the empty mask) and emit one match per ccx/ccz op satisfying R1, R2 or R3, recording the op index, the rewrite id and its replacement ops. Matches are emitted in circuit order and re-propagated after each accepted application, so a cancellation that makes a later control constant is found on the next pass. ANF size is capped (refuse the segment if any wire's monomial set exceeds 4096 terms) so the pass is bounded.
expected_effect: modred_21's non-Clifford content is exactly the 17 ccz (119 = 17 x 7); the 30 h, 24 x and 3 cx are Clifford, and the 'h ccz h' (11x) / 'ccz h x' (14x) trigrams say most ccz are H-sandwiched Toffolis with X-negated controls, i.e. precisely the classical-reversible-with-constants structure these three rewrites read. mod-5^4 reduction compares a register against a constant and conditionally subtracts, so several AND terms are recomputed on wires that already hold them (R2) and several controls are X-negated copies of each other (R1/R3). pyzx reaches 73 T = 119 - 46, i.e. about 6.5 Toffolis' worth, by seeing inside the T-level decomposition; the ANF view gets the same redundancy at the Toffoli level, where the floor's rotation-level Pauli-frame merge is blind because ccz is opaque to it. Conservative estimate: 4 Toffolis removed = 28 T (119 -> 91), with upside to 46 T if every X-negated duplicate fires. No qubits added, no CNOT growth beyond the <= 3 cx replacing a linearised Toffoli, zero error drawn.
source: M. Amy, D. Maslov, M. Mosca, 'Polynomial-time T-depth optimization of Clifford+T circuits via matroid partitioning' (arXiv:1303.2042) and Y. Nam, N. Ross, Y. Su, A. Childs, D. Maslov, 'Automated optimization of large quantum circuits with continuous parameters' (arXiv:1710.07345) - phase/parity propagation through CNOT+Toffoli networks; the GF(2) ANF propagation and idempotent-product cancellation is the standard reversible-logic argument (Soeken-Chattopadhyay, 'Unlocking efficiency and scalability of reversible logic synthesis using conventional logic synthesis', DAC 2016; multiplicative-complexity view in Boyar-Peralta).
